steps: Make the ASL number 9 handshape with both hands, holding only the thumb and index finger out and apart.
Raise both hands to chest height, keeping them a few inches in front of your torso.
Brush the dominant hand's fingertips straight downward across the non-dominant hand's fingertips in one crisp motion.
Point both palms sideways, facing each other, throughout the brushing motion.
Keep your expression neutral and relaxed — the sign is a plain, matter-of-fact comment.
tip: The same sign also means 'simple' or 'easy'; the surrounding sentence tells the reader which sense you mean.

steps: Curl your dominant hand into an E handshape, fingers bent with the thumb tucked beneath them.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your torso, palm facing upward like a tray.
Tap the dominant E hand down onto the non-dominant palm two times, with a short bounce between taps.
Keep the dominant palm facing upward as it lands, so the curled fingers do the tapping.
Hold an assertive, serious expression — this sign presents something as a proven fact.
tip: Swap the E handshape for a flat hand and the sign reads as PROOF instead.

steps: Hold your dominant hand open with all five fingers extended and spread slightly.
Bring the tip of the dominant middle finger up to touch the front of your chin.
Give the chin one firm, quick jab with the fingertip; do not rub or brush across the skin.
Angle the palm inward toward your face so the middle finger points straight at the chin.
Raise your eyebrows slightly and smile a little — the pleased expression marks it as a genuine favorite.
tip: Jab, never brush: a rubbing motion changes the sign into TASTE instead.

steps: Spread your dominant hand into an open 5-handshape with all fingers extended.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat and horizontal at chest height, palm turned toward your torso.
Draw the dominant hand downward across the flat hand while wiggling all four fingers like falling drops.
Face both palms toward your own torso as the dominant hand slides down.
Do the downward wiggle once or twice depending on the sentence — twice suggests a continuing flow.
tip: The wiggling fingers picture blood trickling down; keep the wiggle small and quick so it reads as flow.
